newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Losses to blue chips pull Slovak bourse lower.
newsitem.headline: Losses to blue chips pull Slovak bourse lower.

text.p: Major Slovak shares were mixed in moderate trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange on Wednesday but losses to several blue chips pulled the SAX index down 0.94 points to 195.86.
The biggest net loser among 16 shares in the SAX was the drug producer Slovakofarma, down 199 to 4,101 crowns.

"Such a decline is nothing exceptional as the stock is very iliquid," said Dusan Sykora of ING Barings, adding the Slovakofarma's share could easily gain the same amount the next day as it usualy trades only small volumes which do not indicate longer-term trend.
Steel maker VSZ led trading in terms of volumes, closing unchanged at 745 crowns, and brokers expected its price to hover around the current levels for some time longer.
"There is some demand for VSZ shares which should not let its price fall in coming days, but, on the other hand the demand is not strong enough to pull the price up," Sykora said.

Traders said trading on the BSE remained sluggish as the uncertain Slovak political situation and the turmoil on the neighbouring Czech financial markets keep potential investors away from Bratislava.

"Some foreign investors think the Czech and Slovak Republics are linked more closely than they really are and the Czech problems keep them away from from Slovakia in fears that similar turmoil could also happen here," Sykora said.
He added more lively foreign activity may appear after Slovak referendums on NATO membership and direct presidential elections bring more light to the local political situation.

Overall volume rose to 1,165,068 shares -- boosted by 1,158,530 stocks in direct tardes -- from 142,549 shares traded on Tuesday. Turnover increased to 264.31 million crowns from 26.66 million on Tuesday.
